data.name: Majeed
data.gender_notes: Majeed is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is greater and more exalted than others, possessing high status and majesty. The name Majeed carries the meaning “Majestic, Glorious” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Majeed usually hope their child will grow to embody majestic, glorious and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Refers to Allah's greatness and majesty, and the idea of striving to embody these qualities in one's own life.
data.etymology: Majeed belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Majestic, Glorious.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Majeed total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

It is a name that is often given to those who are held in high esteem in their communities, and it conveys a sense of admiration and respect. In Arabic culture, the name "Majeed" is associated with noble qualities such as generosity, courage, and wisdom. People with this name may be seen as leaders, influencers, and role models.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, the name "Majeed" has a deep spiritual significance. It is a reminder of the greatness and majesty of Allah, the one and only God. The name acknowledges the ultimate power and sovereignty of Allah, and it is a call to recognize and submit to His will. In Islamic teaching, "Majeed" is also associated with the concept of tawheed, or the oneness of God. It is a reminder to focus on the unity of God and to avoid associating any partners or equals with Him. Overall, the name "Majeed" is a powerful reminder of the infinite greatness and majesty of Allah, and it is a call to strive for righteousness and submission to His will.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Majid ibn Harith was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad and one of the early converts to Islam. The name Majeed carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Majid ibn Harith was an Arab nobleman from the tribe of Kinda. He embraced Islam during the early years of the religion and became a close companion of the Prophet Muhammad. He participated in several battles and was known for his bravery and generosity. He is mentioned in several hadiths and is considered a significant figure in early Islamic history.
